browser_eval.rationale: `browser_eval` probes the host with fixed commands (`command -v agent-browser`/`where agent-browser` and `agent-browser --version`) and returns installation/version guidance. The command is not chosen from tool input, so this is not arbitrary host code execution under the HOSTEXEC definition. It does not fetch attacker-controlled content, return host file contents, or send agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

nextjs_call.rationale: `nextjs_call` forwards the chosen `port`, `toolName`, and `args` to a running Next.js runtime MCP tool and returns its raw `result`. The advertised/runtime tools include local application diagnostics such as errors, logs, routes, project metadata, and Server Action source mapping, which are non-public localhost/application data, so it is SECRET. The exact runtime tool outputs vary by Next.js version and are not defined in the provided internal manager code; because returned logs/errors/runtime data can include application/browser/server text whose origin may include third-party or attacker-controllable content, `result` is treated as UNTRUSTED. The tool can also invoke mutating runtime tools such as cache management/clear-cache, so it is classified as WRITE, though the shown code does not establish an attacker-readable SINK or arbitrary HOSTEXEC.

nextjs_docs.rationale: `nextjs_docs` reads local project files under `project_path`/cwd, including `node_modules/next/package.json` and `package.json`, and returns the detected Next.js version/source, local docs path, and docs availability. Those are non-public host/project details, so the tool returns SECRET data. It does not fetch remote documentation or write/send data out.

nextjs_index.rationale: `nextjs_index` discovers/probes local Next.js dev servers and returns local runtime/server information, including port, PID, command, URL, and the MCP tools/input schemas exposed by the dev server. Local process/runtime details and localhost MCP endpoint data are non-public host/application data, so this is SECRET. The shown code does not expose an agent-chosen remote host URL and does not write state. [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]
